{"address":"141fa0730","function_name":"InitializeParticleSpawnRow","comment":"Initialize one native CPU particle row before authored spawn modules run.

Source: SoulcaliburVI.exe141FA0730; CPU sprite vtable143949B60+C8. Caller141FA9E60 supplies emitter, active-index-selected particle storage, position and velocity. Win64 RCX/RDX/R8/R9 verified from assembly.

Algorithm:
1. Clear emitter+110 bytes at the supplied particle row.
2. Copy position into particle+10 and velocity into particle+20 (base) and+30 (current).
3. Subtract emitter+1A8/+1AC/+1B0 from particle position.

Parameters:
pEmitter: native emitter; generic pointer because complete layout is not recovered here.
pParticle: caller-owned particle row, selected from emitter+F0 with stride+114 and index array+F8.
pPosition, pVelocity: read-only three-float vectors. MCP rejected const float* although prototype validation accepted it; stored as float* with read-only semantics documented here.

Returns: void. RAX has no defined semantic return value.

Rollback relevance: receiver141FD3E30 can reach this initializer through forced spawn141F977E0 ->141FA9E60 during completion. Particle+10 is position, +20 is base velocity, +30 is actual velocity; do not describe the+10..2B observer range as complete velocity. Post-spawn141FA0360 uses+30 to integrate+10. The receiver observer separately includes life+0C, both velocities and emitter birth counter+11C. This documents the producer, not complete lifecycle acceptance.

Special Cases: local_res8/local_res10/local_res18 are saved nonvolatile-register slots, not independent state to recover. Bulk undefined8 casts in the decompiler represent pairs of copied floats. Native particle and emitter ownership, bounds and allocation validity are caller preconditions."}
